items.label: LOADER
items.why: the boot program: it loads over the KERNAL's vectors at $02A7-$03FF so that it runs as soon as LOAD prints, shows RAMPAGE and loads the protection stage

items.label: {14}BLOCKS FREE.{00}{00}{00}
items.why: directory art: an entry of two bytes whose name makes the listing end with a false count of blocks free

items.label: LOADER2
items.problem: the chain from (17, 2) loops or leaves the disk
items.why: a decoy directory entry: its chain of sectors loops, so it cannot be loaded, and the loader never asks for it

items.label: PROTECTION
items.problem: the chain from (17, 3) loops or leaves the disk
items.why: a decoy directory entry like LOADER2: its chain loops and nothing asks for it
the protection stage, loaded to $F000: it sends code to the drive, reads one byte back and resets the machine unless it is $C2, then decrypts the code that loads the next stage

items.label: PART1
items.why: the first screen of the load, a program at $C600 that draws the Activision logo and the word PRESENTS; the later files load over it

items.label: PART7
items.why: the two character sets and the explosion's sprite shapes, which lie in the listing at $E000-$F0FF as loaded; the rest of the file, $F100-$F5FF, is zeros and bytes over the first monster's sprite shapes and the screen, which game_start clears

the last loader stage, loaded to $C000. Its first 512 bytes are the loader itself, which the listing does not hold; its second 512 are the first half of the music driver, which the loader copies to $0200-$03FF, where the listing has them

items.label: track 1, sector 1
items.why: six sectors chained in the order 1, 9, 17, 3, 11, 19: a second copy of the protection stage, 1,282 bytes with the load address $C000 where the directory's copy has $F000, and 1,004 bytes the same. No directory entry points at the chain, the loader's loads are all by name, and the protection's drive code reads track 41, not track 1
